MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
FISH ANALYSIS REPORT

Sex: Male
Specimen: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in chronic phase. Patient currently on tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy.

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase FISH analysis using BCR/ABL dual color dual fusion probe (Abbott Molecular)

RESULT: ABNORMAL

BCR/ABL translocation t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) DETECTED

Positive cells: 19/100 (19%)
Normal cells: 81/100 (81%)

INTERPRETATION
Interphase FISH analysis demonstrates the presence of BCR/ABL fusion signals in 19% of cells examined, consistent with the Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)(q34;q11.2). This finding indicates persistent disease despite ongoing TKI therapy.

The dual fusion pattern observed confirms a standard BCR/ABL translocation. The 19% positivity represents a significant disease burden in the context of CML monitoring during treatment.

CLINICAL CORRELATION
This result should be correlated with complete blood count, BCR/ABL quantitative RT-PCR, and clinical assessment. The persistence of 19% BCR/ABL positive cells may indicate suboptimal response to current TKI therapy. Consider BCR/ABL kinase domain mutation analysis if not recently performed.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
